options.content:
Requests to two versions of one service, the stable release and the canary; each sample is one request. The synthetic data runs 250 minutes with 2 series per metric. | column | what it is | values | |---|---|---| | time | Time of the sample | One sample every 5 ms (200 per second) on version stable; one sample every 95 ms (10.53 per second) on version canary | | version | Which version served the request: stable or canary | 2 values: stable, canary | | request_latency | Latency of the request, in seconds | Usual values: Pareto distribution (alpha 3, scale 0.05)
Minutes 30 to 60, ramping in and out over 10 minutes: values multiplied by 1.08 on version canary
Minutes 70 to 110, ramping in and out over 10 minutes: values multiplied by 1.25 on version canary
Minutes 160 to 190: 5% of samples are drawn from a Pareto distribution (alpha 3, scale 2) on version canary
Minutes 200 to 230: 8.7% of samples are random values, uniform between 1 and 1.001 on version canary
Note: never below 0 | | requests | HTTP status code of the request (200 or 500) | Usual values: always 200
Throughout: 0.1% of samples are 500
Minutes 120 to 150: 19.9% of samples are 500 on version canary
Note: whole numbers; each sample's value is stored as the label code |

Each query runs twice, once with the exact plan and once with the approximate plan. A rule reads query results and decides an action; exact and approx decide separately, and the dashboard compares their decisions. On the time charts below, shaded areas are the problem periods injected into the synthetic data.

**Queries**

| query | PromQL | computed |
|---|---|---|
| p99_canary | `quantile_over_time(0.99, request_latency{version="canary"}[5m])` | every 60 s over the last 300 s |
| p95_canary | `quantile_over_time(0.95, request_latency{version="canary"}[5m])` | every 60 s over the last 300 s |
| p99_stable | `quantile_over_time(0.99, request_latency{version="stable"}[5m])` | every 60 s over the last 300 s |
| success_rate_canary | `sum(count_over_time(requests{version="canary", code="200"}[5m])) / sum(count_over_time(requests{version="canary"}[5m]))` | every 60 s over the last 300 s |

**Rules**

| rule | queries it uses | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| ours | p99_canary, p99_stable | A check fails when canary p99 / stable p99 > 1.1. A rollout rolls back when 3 failed checks in a row out of 10; otherwise it promotes. |
| flagger | p99_canary, success_rate_canary | A check fails when canary p99 > 0.5 s or canary success rate < 99%. A rollout rolls back when 10 failed checks in total; promotes after 25 passed checks (up to 34 checks); otherwise it promotes. |
| argo_rollouts | success_rate_canary | A check fails when canary success rate < 95% (a check every 5 evaluations). A rollout rolls back when more than 3 failed checks out of 10; otherwise it promotes. |
| cloudwatch | p99_canary | A check fails when canary p99 > 0.5 s. A rollout rolls back when 4 of the last 5 checks failed, within 10 checks; otherwise it promotes. |
| keptn | p95_canary | A check fails when canary p95 > 1.1 × the mean of the last 3 passing checks, or ≥ 0.6 s (a check every 10 evaluations). A rollout rolls back when the check fails; each check is its own evaluation; otherwise it promotes. |

panels.title: Every run and query: plan, query error, and what the application saw
panels.description: Each row is one query in one run, paired with one rule or alert that reads it; a query read by three rules has three rows. Sketch and parameters are the approximate plan the planner chose: the sketch type and its size (for KMV, k is how many hashes it keeps; for HLL, precision p means 2^p registers). Fidelity compares the rule's decisions on the exact and approx answers: an episode is a stretch of consecutive evaluations where the exact rule fires, an incident is an attack or change the data generator injected (synthetic data only). Hover a fidelity cell to read all of it.

properties.value: Defined per application. Threshold alert: evaluations where exact and approx agree on firing. Autoscaler: matched scaling actions over matched, false and missed ones. Rollout controller: rollouts decided the same. Top clients: mean clients shared by the exact and approx top lists, as a fraction of the list size. Rule: entity-evaluations where exact and approx agree on whether the rule is active.
